root_cause.text: The callee function was writing to `msg_get_inq`, an input-only field from the caller, causing NULL pointer dereference when `state->msg` is NULL during splice operations in `unix_stream_read_generic`, and violating the caller-callee contract by modifying caller-provided state that may not be cleared on struct reuse.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes writes to `msg->msg_get_inq` in both `tcp_recvmsg_locked()` (lines 2655-2656 deleted) and `unix_stream_read_generic()` (lines 2933-2935 deleted), and moves the `do_cmsg` variable declaration inside the `if (msg)` block (line 3089) to prevent dereferencing a potentially NULL `msg` pointer. The commit message explicitly states: "Also avoid NULL pointer dereference in unix_stream_read_generic if state->msg is NULL and msg->msg_get_inq is written. A NULL state->msg can happen when splicing as of commit 2b514574f7e8."

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant or incorrect msg_get_inq assignment that was being set alongside TCP_CMSG_INQ flag.
intent_record.what: Removed the assignment `msg->msg_get_inq = 1;` from inside the `if (tp->recvmsg_inq)` block and changed the block from multi-line to single-line format by removing braces.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the setting of the `msg_get_inq` flag when `recvmsg_inq` is enabled. The TCP_CMSG_INQ flag is still set, but the corresponding message structure field is no longer updated. This may affect how the caller interprets or processes the in-queue notification.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect condition logic by using bitwise OR operators and adding TCP_CMSG_INQ flag check to properly handle inqueue message metadata in TCP receive path.
intent_record.what: Changed two logical OR operators (||) to bitwise OR operators (|) on lines 2930 and 2934. Line 2930: `(cmsg_flags || msg->msg_get_inq)` becomes `(cmsg_flags | msg->msg_get_inq)`. Line 2934: `if (msg->msg_get_inq)` becomes `if ((cmsg_flags & TCP_CMSG_INQ) | msg->msg_get_inq)`.
intent_record.how: The first change alters the condition evaluation from short-circuit logical OR to bitwise OR, which always evaluates both operands and performs bitwise combination instead of boolean logic. The second change adds a bitwise AND operation `(cmsg_flags & TCP_CMSG_INQ)` combined with bitwise OR to `msg->msg_get_inq`, changing the condition from checking only `msg->msg_get_inq` to checking if either the TCP_CMSG_INQ flag is set in cmsg_flags OR msg->msg_get_inq is true. This affects which code path executes for setting msg_inq.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused local variable declaration to clean up dead code in unix_stream_read_generic.
intent_record.what: Removed the declaration of unused variable `bool do_cmsg;` from the `unix_stream_read_generic` function's local variable declarations.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates a variable that was declared but never referenced or assigned within the function body. At runtime, this has no functional impact as the variable was not being used; it only reduces stack frame size marginally and removes dead code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature msg_get_inq initialization that was incorrectly set before proper message processing in unix_stream_read_generic().
intent_record.what: Removed three lines that read the recvmsg_inq flag from the unix socket structure using READ_ONCE(), conditionally set msg_get_inq to 1, and the associated conditional check.
intent_record.how: This change removes the initialization of the msg_get_inq flag based on the socket's recvmsg_inq setting at the start of unix_stream_read_generic(). The flag will no longer be automatically set when entering this function, potentially affecting whether ancillary message queue information is included in the received message.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix inqueue length reporting by checking both per-socket and per-message flags with volatile read to prevent stale cached values.
intent_record.what: Added a new local variable `do_cmsg` initialized with `READ_ONCE(u->recvmsg_inq)`, and changed the condition from `msg->msg_get_inq &&` to `(do_cmsg | msg->msg_get_inq) &&` using bitwise OR instead of logical AND.
intent_record.how: This change modifies the control flow for setting `msg->msg_inq`. Previously, the condition required `msg->msg_get_inq` to be true. Now it succeeds if either `do_cmsg` (from `u->recvmsg_inq`) OR `msg->msg_get_inq` is set. The `READ_ONCE()` macro ensures the kernel reads `u->recvmsg_inq` fresh from memory, preventing compiler optimizations that might cache the value. This allows the inqueue length to be reported via either the per-socket `recvmsg_inq` flag or the per-message `msg_get_inq` flag.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The root cause was that the code was unconditionally writing to msg->msg_get_inq and posting SCM_INQ cmsg based on either u->recvmsg_inq OR msg->msg_get_inq. The fix changes the logic in three ways: (1) It introduces a do_cmsg flag that is set only based on u->recvmsg_inq (line 2933: 'do_cmsg = READ_ONCE(u->recvmsg_inq)'), (2) It only sets msg->msg_get_inq if do_cmsg is true (lines 2934-2935), preventing unconditional modification of caller-provided state, and (3) It changes the condition from 'READ_ONCE(u->recvmsg_inq) || msg->msg_get_inq' to 'msg->msg_get_inq && (copied ?: err) >= 0' (line 3095), ensuring cmsg is only posted when do_cmsg is true (line 3097-3098). This prevents NULL pointer dereference when state->msg is NULL and respects the caller-callee contract by not modifying msg->msg_get_inq unless explicitly requested via u->recvmsg_inq.
